Mike, Axiom/Mir, Codex, and Mirror; equal 260 max / 178 acceleration / 2.45 turn; +7.5 percent catch-up ceiling; 85 percent attack-heavy race pool; repairable three-segment Flux Guard; and server authority remained non-negotiable.

The second full-suite attempt rejected a stale Signal Tour test assertion that still expected state schema v6. The test was corrected to v7 while retaining the forward-only tour lock and all tour/frozen-mechanic checks.

The complete V20 suite passed 36 focused checks, 45,504 interpolation poses and 864 snaps, 108,000 kinetic poses, reflection routes, Mirror Echo V2, 108,000 target-recorder samples, 101 LAN snapshots, managed bind/private-interface self-probe, 24 default races, 36 track races, 72 variant races, 32 battles, Signal Tour, reliability, restart recovery, and HTTP.

A unique start action entered a visible 3 countdown and active reversed four-racer play. The natural result reached MIRROR WINS and named Prism Wraith // MIRROR FORGE // REFLECTION RUN // CLEAR SIGNAL // 3 LAPS with all four rankings.

Live authority geometry preserved point zero at x 1101.27 y 400. Reflection point one was x 1095.9 y 390.17, exactly the canonical forward final point, independently corroborating actual reversed traversal rather than renamed copy.

Mirror sealed a reflection lap at 0:10.259. RUN IT BACK retained reflection; axm.mirror-echo/v2 reported sealed with one direction-specific record and rendered the labelled non-colliding echo while all four authoritative racers remained present.

At an explicit 390x844 responsive browser viewport, the first visible Echo HUD overlapped the P4 standings row. The mobile Echo HUD top offset moved from 144 px to 178 px; after reload and a new reflection run, P4 ended at y 227 and Echo began at y 247 with an empty overlap set.

The corrected 390x844 browser composition had document width/height exactly 390x844, four standings, three Flux Guard segments, five touch controls, reflection HUD, and a visible Mirror Echo without clipping or overlap. This remained responsive browser evidence only, not a physical phone or touch claim.

Final 1280x720 reflection racing sampled 240 render frames at 2.32 ms average and 3.4 ms p95 total work; track averaged 0.4 ms, actors 0.53 ms, UI 0.74 ms average and 1.2 ms p95; 423 interpolation frames accrued with zero snaps. schedulerLimited was true, so no target cadence or 60 fps claim was admitted.

Warning/error logs were empty. The available browser surface provided repeated stills and semantic state but no rolling visual buffer; high-cadence reflection, echo, and kinetic motion therefore remained UNKNOWN. No screenshot/video file was created or retained.

content.routes.reflection and direction-isolated content.replay.mirror-echo were admitted at bounded local contracts. The regenerated comparator remained UNKNOWN overall with zero missing declarations; physical, performance, audio/human, breadth, and steward gates did not change state.

The latest accelerated 30-virtual-minute rotation recorded 1800 acknowledged actions, 59 resumes, 12 settled results, zero rejected resumed actions, and 5.9 MB observed heap delta; this is not a real-time target soak.

Focused game-package verification returned zero errors and one expected physical-phone warning. The package-verifier selftest passed 15 assertions, the capability-comparator selftest passed, and all 21 lane JSON files parsed.

The final read-only Game Hub snapshot scanned 2,023 files, found 208 recent and 81 active files, and reported one active shared seam only in foreign 018 game.manifest.json. Lane-015 package, manifest, and evidence seams were re-read; no foreign 014/016/017/018 file was edited.

The temporary loopback V20 verification authority on port 8825 was intentionally stopped, the browser viewport reset, and its tab finalized. No V20 runtime is intentionally left active; future port state is ephemeral and must be health-checked against current source.

The production-stewardship goal remains open. Four real phones on the intended router for 30 minutes, representative target-hardware 30-minute performance and high-cadence observation, human listening/mix/attachment/replay/route preference, broader animation/voice/content, and explicit steward approval remain unproven; no AAA achievement is claimed.
